text:
sara_ml: CI failing on onboarding run for orion-13b-q4f — runner timed out in collate step. logs show token counts way higher than expected, causing batching to explode. anyone seen this? :eyes:

kai: can you paste the failing log snippet and the exact eval config you used?

sara_ml: sure — here's the tail of the job log:
```
2026-05-12T14:02:33Z collate.py:INFO expected_max_tokens=2048
2026-05-12T14:02:33Z collate.py:ERROR batch_tokens=8192 input_samples=4
2026-05-12T14:02:33Z runner.py:WARN waiting_for_kv_cache_flush (120s)
2026-05-12T14:02:33Z runner.py:ERROR timed out during collate step
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "./runner.py", line 312, in run
    collated = collate(samples)
  File "./collate.py", line 78, in collate
    raise CollateError(f"batch_tokens {total_tokens} > max {max_tokens}")
CollateError: batch_tokens 8192 > max 2048
```
config snippet:
```
model: orion-13b-q4f
template: chatpad
max_seq: 2048
quant: q4f
```
One weird detail: the failing batch contains prompts with emojis + a system message that gets duplicated in the template output.

dmitri: that duplication rings a bell — we recently changed chatpad rendering to fallback to a generic system message when the template missing `system` key. if both template and fallback are applied you can end up with duplicate system/assistant sentinels which inflate token counts. also note: some tokenizers (esp. multibyte emoji sequences) tokenise into many subtokens which multiplies the effect.

samira: I reproduced locally. Minimal repro attached: tests/repro.json (contains one user prompt with long emoji sequence + chatpad template). Command I ran:
```
./eval_runner --model orion-13b-q4f --template chatpad --input tests/repro.json --max_seq 2048
```
It fails in collate with same error. Quick hack: trimming duplicate system blocks in template renderer avoids the blowup.

eval-bot: CI job #4729 failed — https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4729 — failing step: eval-onboard-orion-13b-q4f

kai: two actionable things here: 1) short-term: add a guard in collate to cap per-sample tokens and produce a clearer validation error (and bump onboarding job timeout to 3m so we don't hit flaky timeouts). 2) medium-term: add a tokenizer smoke-test to model onboarding that runs tokenizer.encode on a small corpus (including emojis, CJK, ZWJ sequences) and compares lengths against a heuristic. that would catch models with unexpected tokenizer behavior.

sara_ml: confirm trim_system=True in template rendering fixed my local run. I'll open a PR with the template guard + unit test. also adding tokenizer_smoke to the orion model config seems sensible.

dmitri: please also update the onboarding checklist: require `tokenizer:name` and `sentinel_tokens` in model config. If missing, the onboarding job should fail fast with a clear message.

samira: should we apply the template fix to other chat templates (assistant-v2, assistant-compact)? looks like that code path is shared.

kai: yes, backport to the other templates and add a small collate unit that asserts batch_tokens <= max_seq * batch_size. If assertion fails, include sample hashes so we can repro from logs.

sara_ml: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/pulls/2345 — fixes template duplication, adds tokenizer_smoke flag to model config, and a collate guard. added a short unit test using tests/repro.json. marking for review. (:bug: @dmitri @samira please take a look)

samira: looking now. if CI passes, we should also add a short note to the eval-harness README about emoji edgecases and quantized tokenizer differences.

dmitri: acked. once merged we'll re-run the onboarding job for orion-13b-q4f. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
